description: Reads and writes the issues, pull requests and repositories of GitHub and GitLab through one interface: a thread with its comments (and, for a pull request, its branches, CI checks, reviews and changed files), a repository's metadata, the issues of a repository; and creates issues, labels and pull requests, comments, edits, closes, reopens, reviews and merges. Without a form flag it reads and changes nothing. Every write is listed in side_effects; --dry-run makes the reads and none of the writes. The token comes from the environment.

input.description: At most one reference: an issue or pull request (a web URL, owner/repo#N, owner/repo!N for a pull or merge request, or N, #N, !N in the repository of the origin remote of --dir), or a repository (owner/repo, group/subgroup/project, a repository or git remote URL). The forms that take a repository use the origin remote's when none is given.

add-label.description: with --edit, a label to add; repeated or comma-separated

assignee.description: an assignee: of the issue to open, or the thread's new assignees with --edit; repeated or comma-separated. With --list, the one assignee to filter by. The GitLab client does not send assignees

base.description: with --create-pr, the branch to merge into

body.description: the body: of the issue, comment, pull request or review, the thread's new body with --edit, or the comment --close posts first

body-file.description: read the body from this file; - is stdin. Not with --body

checks.description: with the read of a pull request, also read the CI checks of its head commit

close.description: the close form: close the thread, after a comment when --body or --body-file is given; a closed thread is left as it is

color.description: with --create-label, the label's colour as six hex digits (ededed); default the forge's on GitHub, ededed on GitLab

comment.description: the comment form: comment on the thread; the body is --body or --body-file

commit-message.description: with --merge, the message of the merge commit

commit-title.description: with --merge, the title of the merge commit

create.description: the create form: open an issue in the repository with --title (required), --body or --body-file, --label and --assignee

create-label.description: the create-label form: create the label of this name in the repository, with --color and --description; one that exists already is not an error

create-pr.description: the create-pr form: open a pull or merge request from --head into --base with --title, --body or --body-file, and --draft

dir.description: the git working tree whose origin remote names the repository when the input does not

direction.description: with --list, the order: asc or desc

draft.description: with --create-pr, open it as a draft

dry-run.description: with a write form, make its reads and none of its writes, and list the writes in result.planned

edit.description: the edit form: change the thread's --title, --body, --assignee, and --add-label and --remove-label; a body cannot be emptied

files.description: with the read of a pull request, also read the files it changes

forge.description: the forge, github or gitlab, for when it cannot be told from the input, the environment or the origin remote

head.description: with --create-pr, the branch to merge from

label.description: a label: of the issue to open, or a filter of --list (an issue must have every one); repeated or comma-separated

limit.description: with --list, the most issues to list; incomplete is true when more match

list.description: the list form: the issues of the repository, pull requests left out, filtered by --state, --label and --assignee, ordered by --sort and --direction, at most --limit

merge.description: the merge form: merge the pull request with --method, at --sha, with --commit-title and --commit-message

method.description: with --merge, the merge method: merge, squash or rebase; default the forge's (on GitHub, the first the repository allows)

remove-label.description: with --edit, a label to remove; repeated or comma-separated. One the thread does not have is not an error

reopen.description: the reopen form: reopen the thread; an open thread is left as it is

review.description: the review form: post a review comment on the pull request; the body is --body or --body-file

reviews.description: with the read of a pull request, also read its reviews

sha.description: with --merge, the head commit the pull request must be at, or the merge is refused

sort.description: with --list, order by: created or updated

state.description: with --list, the issues in this state: open, closed or all

timeout.description: the longest the whole call may take

title.description: the title: of the issue or pull request to open, or the thread's new title with --edit

tool.description: the command that wrote this envelope

ok.description: true only when the command did the whole job it was asked to do; never true beside a non-zero exit_code or an error

status.description: the outcome in words, derived from exit_code: done (0), failed (1) or usage (2)

exit_code.description: the process exit code: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 usage error

summary.description: one sentence on the outcome, at most 200 characters

error.description: what failed and where; present exactly when ok is false

category.description: the kind of failure, which says whether re-running could help; an open set

retryable.description: whether re-running the identical command could succeed

resumable.description: whether re-running the same input continues the work rather than starting it over

fix_hint.description: a mechanical remedy, where one is known

env.description: the environment variables, one of which supplies what is missing

valid.description: the values the flag accepts here

warnings.description: what went differently than intended without stopping the call

code.description: a stable code naming the cause; an open set

severity.description: high when the result is not quite what it appears to be, low when informational

forge.description: the forge the call went to: github or gitlab

repo.description: the repository, owner/name; a GitLab owner may hold subgroups

host.description: the repository's web host, when the input or the origin remote named one

ref.description: the thread: owner/name#N for an issue, owner/name!N for a pull or merge request; runnable as the input of the next call

issue.description: the issue, or the issue view of a pull request: title, body, state, labels, author

comments.description: the thread's comments, oldest first; [] when it has none. Read forms only

comments_truncated.description: the thread has more comments than were read (the client reads at most 500)

pull_request.description: the pull or merge request: branches, head commit, draft and merged

checks.description: with --checks, the CI checks of the head commit

reviews.description: with --reviews, the reviews of the pull request

files.description: with --files, the files the pull request changes

repository.description: the repository: default branch, visibility, the caller's permissions and the merge methods allowed

issues.description: with --list, the issues that match, without pull requests; [] when none does

incomplete.description: with --list, more issues match than --limit allowed

comment_url.description: with --comment, the web URL of the comment

label.description: with --create-label, the label asked for; a label that already existed is not an error

merge.description: with --merge, the forge's answer: merged, the merge commit and its message

no_change.description: the thread was already in the state asked for (--close on a closed one, --reopen on an open one); nothing was written

dry_run.description: the call ran under --dry-run: nothing was written, and planned lists what would have been

planned.description: under --dry-run, the writes the call would have made, in order

action.description: what would be written, as SideEffect.Action

kind.description: what it would be written to: issue, pull_request or repository

target.description: the thread or the repository it would be written to

detail.description: what it would carry, in words: the fields, labels or method

side_effects.description: every write to a forge, in the order it was made, a failed one included

action.description: what was written: create_issue, comment, edit, add_labels, remove_label, close, reopen, create_label, create_pull_request, review or merge

kind.description: what it was written to: issue, pull_request or repository

target.description: the thread (owner/repo#N, owner/repo!N) or the repository (owner/repo) written to

url.description: the web URL of what the write made, when the forge returned one

ok.description: whether the forge accepted the write

warning.description: the warning raised about this write, if any

next.description: the invocations a caller would plausibly make next

input.description: its one positional input; empty when the call takes none

flags.description: the flags to add, each value its own element

why.description: why a caller would run it

duration_ms.description: wall-clock time of the call, in milliseconds

started_at.description: when the call started, RFC 3339 in UTC

exit_codes.0: done: read, or written, or nothing needed to change
exit_codes.1: failed: the stage and category are named in error (auth, input, conflict, api, aborted); side_effects lists the writes made before the failure
exit_codes.2: usage error: the call is refused before anything is written
